newsitem.title: USA: Cinton, Blair condemn Belfast bomb.
newsitem.headline: Cinton, Blair condemn Belfast bomb.

text.p: DENVER, June 21 (Reuter) U.S. President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Saturday condemned a car bombing in central Belfast that occurred as Group of Seven leaders met in Denver to discuss global issues, including terrorism.

"This is another appalling terrorism act and it simply underlines the need to move this (Northern Ireland peace) process forward," Blair told reporters as he met Clinton on the sidelines of the summit.
The explosion came at a tense time in Northern Ireland following the murder last week of two policemen by the Irish Republican Army.
Both Blair and Clinton stressed that IRA violence must be stopped if its political wing, Sinn Fein, was to be accepted at peace talks.

Clinton said: "I deplore this act today, but I frankly think now the ball is in Sinn Fein's court." He added: "Everybody has decisions to make in life. Their decision is, are they going to be part of this peace process or not. I hope the answer will be yes."

Blair, who wants to persuade Americans to stop supporting the IRA, said: "What is essential is for Sinn Fein and everyone else to realise that if they want to be part of this process they have got to engage in purely democratic means."
